data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A small research team should adopt an existing experiment tracker only if their workflow is purely observational; however, if the research involves active learning loops where the tracker must function as a real-time controller modifying experimental parameters, they must build a custom minimal tracker to avoid the 'integration tax' of hacking additive tools into a causal role.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The team's active learning requirements are trivial enough to be scripted externally without tight integration.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"An existing open-source tool already exposes a native bidirectional control API matching the specific research domain.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The team has sufficient engineering bandwidth to maintain a custom state machine without distracting from core research goals.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Causal Role Separation: Existing tools are architected as passive ledgers (additive to cognitive bandwidth), whereas active learning requires a bidirectional control loop. Forcing a passive ledger to act as a controller introduces a 'migration cliff' and unstructured data noise because the tool lacks a native schema for state-machine transitions. A custom build enforces a mechanist causal model where every metric maps directly to a control action, eliminating the fragility of a single point of failure created by wrapping mismatched systems.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
